title: India Fires Advanced Agni Missile With Multiple Warheads
excerpt: DRDO's May 8 MIRV test proves one missile can strike several targets across the Indian Ocean simultaneously.
body:
India conducted the successful flight-trial of an Advanced Agni missile with a Multiple Independently Targeted Re-Entry Vehicle (MIRV) system from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha, on May 8, 2026. The missile carried multiple payloads aimed at different targets spread across a large geographical area in the Indian Ocean Region. The test, confirmed by both DRDO and the Ministry of Defence, places India firmly among the world's most capable strategic missile powers.

**What MIRV technology actually means:**
Unlike conventional ballistic missiles that carry a single warhead, a MIRV-capable missile can carry several warheads and release them at different targets during the re-entry phase — in simple terms, one missile can strike multiple locations simultaneously. Telemetry and tracking was carried out by multiple ground- and ship-based stations that monitored the entire missile trajectory from lift-off to impact, with flight data confirming that all mission objectives were met.

**Why this matters strategically:**
Since India follows a doctrine of credible minimum deterrence and a no-first-use policy, MIRV capability will significantly strengthen its second-strike ability to retaliate even after absorbing a first attack. With MIRV capability, India joins a small group of countries possessing this technology — including the United States, Russia, China, France, and the United Kingdom — widely regarded as a hallmark of mature strategic nuclear forces. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, the Indian Army, and industry, saying 'This will add an incredible capability to the country's defence preparedness against the growing threat perceptions.'

**What to watch next:**
DRDO chairman Samir V. Kamat has confirmed the organization is ready to conduct a 10,000km-plus Agni-6 test and is awaiting government clearance — making the authorization of that next-generation ICBM the most consequential decision on India's strategic horizon.
